verdict.rationale: Superpowers workflows are git-native — worktrees, PR/merge choices at the end of implementation, and a documented refusal to force-delete uncommitted work protect against destructive rollback of code changes (superpowers-docs-4, superpowers-docs-12, superpowers-docs-41, superpowers-docs-47). Subagent/self-review loops (superpowers-docs-6, superpowers-comm-3) provide 'review' of automation output. However there's no evidence of versioning or rollback for the skills/automations themselves (e.g., pinning or reverting a skill to a prior version, viewing skill change history for the user's own automations) — missing for 10: skill/automation version history, explicit rollback-to-prior-version tooling, and independent confirmation that git-worktree rollback works reliably in practice.
